taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Anatherum glomeratum. Andropogon glomeratus is retained as the primary familiar alias because Texas field guides and local floras still overwhelmingly use it.
look_here_first: Start with the fluffy head. Bushy bluestem makes dense broomlike to cottony clusters near the top of the plant, with paired short rames packed inside and emerging from upper leaf sheaths. The inflorescence looks bushy rather than like separate turkey-foot fingers.

project_inclusion.range_basis: UT Plant Resources Center North Hays County long-term grassland account; documented Travis County LBJ Wildflower Center occurrence; detailed Williamson County species treatment under synonym Andropogon glomeratus.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Synonym-based county records are counted only because Kew explicitly treats Andropogon glomeratus as a synonym of Anatherum glomeratum.

best_field_traits: upper canopy packed with many dense inflorescence units
paired short rames with long silky hairs
upper inflorescence branches partly concealed by leaflike/bract sheaths
often associated with moist low sites and drainage edges
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Big bluestem has a few clean digitate racemes; broomsedge has narrower, more individually sheath-enclosed silky racemes. Bushy bluestem has the densest broad brushlike crown.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Big bluestem has a few clean digitate racemes; broomsedge has narrower, more individually sheath-enclosed silky racemes. Bushy bluestem has the densest broad brushlike crown.
